title: introduce-model-collation-and-release-snippet-generator
author: Nora Patel
release_notes: Adds model collation hints, a deterministic release snippet generator, and compact perf-profile signing. Enables automated concise release blurbs and delta-aware notes for model version rollouts.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a small extensible framework for producing compact, privacy-safe release snippets for model onboarding and profile updates.

Motivation: release note automation for the model registry had two recurring problems: 1) generated notes were noisy and repeated low-value metadata, and 2) performance profiles often contained large tables or raw telemetry that shouldn't be surfaced verbatim.

This change introduces: 1) a lightweight 'collation hints' schema which annotates model/profile changes with human-facing tags (e.g., 'latency-regression', 'quantization-tweak', 'compat-compatibility-add') and a short 'context' string to seed templated blurbs; 2) a deterministic snippet composer that consumes collation hints + profile deltas and emits a concise blurb, confidence score, and suggested follow-ups; 3) compact-profile signer that canonicalizes and signs a small JSON representation of perf profiles so release tooling can reference a signed artifact rather than embedding raw telemetry; 4) small CLI and web UI hooks to preview generated snippets and accept/override suggestions.

Checklist:
- [x] design collation-hints schema and validator
- [x] implement snippet composer with template fallback
- [x] add compact profile serializer + signing utility
- [x] wire preview endpoint to registry UI
- [x] add unit + integration tests
- [x] update docs and quickstart

Notes on privacy: compact profile serialization omits raw logs and sample inputs; it stores aggregated histograms and peak-watermarks only.

Design decisions:
- Collation hints are intentionally minimal (tags + short context) so product writers can edit blurbs easily.
- Composer uses a small templating DSL and a confidence heuristic based on delta magnitude and signal coverage.
- Signer uses the existing release key service; signer output is a short base64 signature and a canonicalized content hash.

Review thread (condensed):
- Samir Gupta (reviewer): "Overall LGTM. Two concerns: (1) how do we avoid leaking sample inputs in the compact profile? (2) Can we make the composer fail open if confidence is low?"
- Nora (author): "(1) Compact serializer intentionally drops raw examples; only percentiles and counts are retained. See serializer/compact_profile.py comments. (2) Composer returns an explicit 'confidence' field; preview UI will show warnings and keeps manual accept path. I've added tests for the fallback path."
- Eve Liang (reviewer): "Please add a short migration note for existing release automation that expects full profiles."
- Nora: "Added docs/examples and a non-breaking compatibility shim: existing pipelines can request 'full_profile=true' until they migrate."
- Marta Reyes (reviewer): "Can we include a per-snippet provenance token so we can trace who edited the suggested blurb?"
- Nora: "Added 'editor' and 'origin' fields to the snippet envelope; signer ensures the envelope is tamper-evident."

Post-merge actions:
- Backfill a small script to generate preview snippets for the last 30 model releases (ENG-7291)
- Add a short runbook for PR reviewers to look for low-confidence snippets when approving rollouts
- Add usage telemetry to track when generated snippets are accepted vs edited

Migration notes: Existing release automation that consumed the old profile payload should switch to the compact-profile endpoint; we provide a compatibility flag and a deprecation timeline of 6 months.

Impact/risk: Low-medium. The change is additive and protected behind a feature flag in the web UI and CLI. Tests cover the signer path and fallback heuristics. Merge: squash-merged into main.
